items.rationale: The in-car impact is covered under §§2.6.2 and 4.5.2, and the battery health waiver disapplies §2.6.8. The supplier's report supports replacement under §7.1.10; estimated equivalent new cost of €800 less €50 in salvage gives €750, before any undisclosed event deductible or sub-limit.
Section 7.1.9 limits payment to the equivalent pre-loss specification, which is priced separately on line 1. The elective upgrade difference is excluded.

The cracked screen is covered impact damage under §§2.6.2–2.6.4; the tablet is assessed separately but shares the laptop's event deductible. Allow about €180 gross for a like-for-like screen repair, subject to the equivalent replacement ceiling in §7.1.10.

Section 5.2.3 covers necessary diagnostics on both units, including the laptop found uneconomic to repair. Allow €45 per device, or €90 gross in total, below the shared €250 event cap and subject to deduction of any credit against the repair.
Under §§4.2.6 and 7.1.5, a carrying case is assessed separately and is not covered merely because the laptop was damaged. The bag was not damaged in the incident.
Sections 3.5(f) and 7.1.8(e) exclude warranties and other undertakings as to future performance, even when purchased with a covered replacement.
Sections 3.5(d) and 4.3(c) exclude data recovery unless separately scheduled. The battery health waiver does not provide that extension.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes separate administrative charges, including those billed by another provider engaged on the claim. The fee also relates to excluded data recovery.
